recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-16373 unless FHIR-I chooses to reopen broader reference-resolvability policy.
issue_request: FHIR-16373 was a Published FHIR-core references-page clarification raised against STU3. It asked to replace "allowing for access control, temporary unavailability, etc." in the literal-reference rule with wording that says references are resolvable "given that access control works, there is no temporary unavailability, etc."; Jira resolved it as Persuasive with "Fix as proposed."
initial_application: The Jira application comment "svn revision 14237" maps to git-svn commit 972f748261828fa2352fc3b0d546a979819b795a, whose git-svn-id ends in build@14237. That commit changed source/references.html from the "allowing for" phrase to the proposed "given that access control works, there is no temporary unavailability, etc" wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps the Reference type page to references.html, so source/references.html is current build-scoped source for the literal-reference narrative. The current source still states that references SHALL point to an actual FHIR resource and be resolvable "given that access control works, there is no temporary unavailability, etc." Later same-page edits added canonical-resolution detail and editorial spelling/punctuation changes but did not reverse the approved clarification. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant discussion or conflicting work-group evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch now has a single empty audit commit for FHIR-16373 because the current build-scoped source already carries the approved clarification and no later evidence found in this bounded investigation requires a different rule.
